title: introduce-auth-tactician-ttl-prefetch-and-pullstream-refactor
author: Ethan Park
description: Context: Cross-SDK follow-up to earlier session/lease work — introduces an "auth tactician" component that centralizes token TTL awareness and a small prefetch policy to avoid tail latency for streamed pull/push APIs. Motivation: customers saw intermittent ~200-400ms spikes when long-running streams triggered last-second token refreshes; retry/backoff logic masked this but increased request churn and observable noise. Goal: reduce tail latency by proactively warming credentials within a TTL window, provide a small, well-documented opt-in prefetch policy across Python/TS/Go SDKs, and clean up PullStream ergonomics so the language SDKs expose a common surface for cancellable/asynchronous consumption. What I changed: 1) auth/tactician: new minimal stateful component (Python: redwood_sdk.session.tactician, TS: auth/tactician.ts, Go: session/tactician.go) that tracks token TTLs, schedules a single prefetch per session when TTL < configured window, and exposes hooks for the SDK session factories to opt into warm-up; 2) prefetch policy: defaults to disabled for backwards compatibility, opt-in via SDK session config as prefetch_window_ms and prefetch_enabled; adds telemetry events (tactician.prefetch.scheduled, tactician.prefetch.success, tactician.prefetch.error); 3) PullStream refactor: unified pullstream interface name changes (Python: PullAsync -> PullStreamAsync, TS: PullStream class tidy, Go: PullIterator improvements) and clarified cancellation semantics in all three SDKs; 4) retries interplay: small change to retry predicate so a refresh in-flight counts as a non-retryable transient state for a single attempt to avoid double-refresh races; 5) docs and examples: migration guide, prefetch demo, and updated version notes for Python/TS/Go SDK releases. Compatibility notes: all changes are opt-in and default behavior is preserved; SDK minor bumps included to expose the new options (py 2.7.0, ts 1.18.0, go 1.5.0). Testing: unit tests around tactician scheduling and backoff, integration tests that run a long-lived PullStream while forcing token TTL expiry, and end-to-end scenario against a staging control-plane that simulates delayed token issuance. Rollout plan: feature flagged server-side and SDK flags default off; enable in canary customers after 2 weeks smoke. Checklist: [x] add tactician implementations across three SDKs [x] add telemetry and docs [x] add integration tests [x] add version bumps and changelogs [x] run cross-SDK regression job
commits: initial: add tactician interface and python impl; ts: implement tactician + expose prefetch config; go: session tactician + iterator changes; docs: add prefetch guide and examples; tests: integration test for stream w/ forced ttl expiry; fix: reconcile type names and update changelogs
review_thread: Aisha: +1 on overall approach; can we keep prefetch disabled by default? Also request clearer metric names for integration with Console. Ethan: Prefetch default is false; added telemetry prefixes tactician.prefetch.* and included mapping in docs. Luca: I think the TS PullStream rename might be breaking for some consumers; would prefer an alias export to maintain ergonomics. Ethan: Added export alias PullAsync -> PullStream in TS package entrypoint to preserve import paths. Riley: go iterator change looks good but please add comment about thread-safety of the tactician scheduling state. Ethan: Added sync.Mutex guard and a unit test simulating concurrent Close/Refresh. Aisha: CI flaked once on the e2e test due to timeouts. Ethan: increased test timeout and added retry logic in the harness; reran CI. Final: approvals from Aisha and Luca; Riley left an approving comment after the mutex test landed.
release_notes: Added an opt-in auth 'tactician' that can prefetch credentials shortly before expiry to reduce stream-tail latency. New SDK config: prefetch_enabled (bool), prefetch_window_ms (int). PullStream naming unified across SDKs; TS maintains backward-compatible exports. Minor SDK bumps: py 2.7.0, ts 1.18.0, go 1.5.0.
notes_for_release_manager: This change is behind SDK and server-side feature flags. Do not enable globally until smoke tests for canary customers pass. Coordinate coordinated release: publish SDKs (py/ts/go) in same day and update Console mapping for tactician telemetry.
post_merge_tasks: publish python wheel, npm publish typescript package, go module tag, update SDK samples repo, enable flag for 5% canary, monitor tactician.prefetch.* metrics for error rates
ci_log_summary: CI: lint/format OK; unit tests PASS; integration tests flaky first run (timeout) then PASS after timeout bump; e2e staging puzzle: one run had 502 from staging auth service simulated delay, rerun passed.
testing_summary: Unit coverage: tactician scheduling, retry predicate interaction, pullstream cancellation; Integration: simulated TTL expiry while a long-lived stream is open; End-to-end: validated streaming latency tail reduction in staging with prefetch_enabled=true (median tail reduced from 320ms to 60ms in controlled run).
priority_notes: Opt-in feature; prioritized for SRE/Platform customers reporting stream tail spikes. Not a breaking change but version bumps required to access new flags.
